statement: Micron says the 512GB RDIMM cuts operating power by more than 60% versus four 128GB RDIMMs (16.0W against 44.2W) and delivers up to 1.4x higher performance on Spark SVM analytics versus 256GB DDR5.
why: Power per terabyte of memory is part of the same fixed-power arithmetic that governs how much accelerator capacity a site can host.

impact.mechanism: Consolidating four modules into one lowers memory-subsystem draw, freeing power budget inside the rack for compute.

evidence.excerpt: the 512GB RDIMM reduces operating power by more than 60% compared with four 128GB RDIMMs, based on 16.0W for one 512GB module versus 44.2W total for four 128GB modules
up to 1.4x higher performance for Spark SVM-based analytics versus 256GB DDR5

confidence.basis: Vendor-supplied benchmark figures in a press release, single secondary publisher, no independent verification.

dispersion: Power claim is module-level (16.0W vs 44.2W); the 1.4x performance claim is workload-specific to Spark SVM analytics.
